submitted.rationale: Of the three compositions measured, index 28 (Cu0.096Sb0.904) had the highest EQE: 0.00277%. That is about 100 times the other two, which were at the noise floor. Pure CuSb2O6 (index 16) gave essentially zero, and so did the Cu-rich multi-phase film (index 5). This suggests that dilute Cu in a wide-gap Sb oxide works better than the stoichiometric or Cu-rich phases.

rejected.reason: Single-phase CuSb2O6 (on the MACE hull) measured EQE of about -8.6e-5%, effectively zero.
Cu-rich multi-phase film measured EQE of about 2.1e-5%, effectively zero.

consultations.verdict: Support: MACE puts CuSb2O6 (mp-5831) on the hull (0.0001 eV/atom), and index 16 sits at its stoichiometry (Cu 0.315). The XRD looks like a single phase. The MEGNet HSE gap of 0.02 eV is not believable for a Cu2+ d9 antimonate (DFT gets this wrong; experiment gives about 1.5-2 eV), so I treat the gap as uninformative. Measuring the stable ternary is a sound anchor.

Uninformative. MEGNet gives CuO a gap of about 0 eV, the same underestimate it made for CuSb2O6, so the gap model can't separate candidates here. Pure CuSb2O6 (index 16) gave zero EQE. Index 5 is Cu-rich and its XRD shows a different, multi-phase pattern (likely CuO plus a Cu-Sb oxide). That is the untested regime, so I'm measuring it on experimental grounds.

Mixed. MEGNet gives Sb2O3 an HSE gap of 3.77 eV, which is above the 2.4 eV illumination, so the Sb oxide matrix alone won't absorb. At the Sb-rich end, though, absorption would come from dilute Cu2+ / CuSb2O6 inside a wide-gap antimony oxide, which could still help charge separation. The GP's UCB picks this unexplored end, and the other two regions measured about zero. I'm taking the best remaining untested regime.
